statement: A film lasts 1 hour. Mia has watched half of it. How many minutes of the film are left?

choices.misconception: I found a quarter of an hour instead of half of it.
I mixed up half and a quarter, so I took 15 minutes away from 60.
I thought one hour has 100 minutes, so half of it is 50.
I gave the length of the whole film, not the part that is left.

hints: How many minutes are in one hour?
Change the hour into minutes first. Watching half means the part left is the other half, so the part left is the same size as the part watched.
One hour is 60 minutes. Half of 60 is the part watched, and the same amount is left.

solutions.reliable: One hour is 60 minutes. Half of 60 is 30, so Mia has watched 30 minutes and $60 - 30 = 30$ minutes are left. The idea to keep: change hours into minutes before finding a fraction of the time.
solutions.elegant: The two halves of anything are equal, so the part left is also half: 30 minutes.

whyOnTest: Finding half of an hour checks both the fraction and the unit, since an hour is 60 minutes and not 100.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
